site.name: Marshall / Langford–Gorham Coal Camp & Mine Complex
site.location: Marshall / Marshall Mesa / South Boulder Creek
site.category: Coal Mining Camp / Mine / Railroad Complex
overview: Marshall was one of Boulder County's earliest coal-mining communities. Coal mining began here in the 1860s, and during the 1860s and 1870s the camp grew rapidly enough that its population exceeded Boulder's.

The Marshall landscape preserves the story of a coal camp, underground workings, mine-support buildings and transportation connections. Historic county sources identify the Fox Mine and Marshall Mesa as surviving reference points for this larger mining landscape.

timeline.text: Coal was discovered near Marshall in 1859, and Boulder County records place the beginning of coal mining in the Boulder-Weld Coal Field at Marshall in 1864.
Coal mining prospered at Marshall, and Boulder County's historic-site survey notes that the camp's population exceeded Boulder's during this period.
The surviving Fox Mine Office dates to 1883; Boulder County records the Fox Mine as operating from 1884 until 1936.
The Boulder-Weld coal field around Marshall remained actively drift-mined into 1939, leaving extensive underground workings beneath the modern open-space landscape.

moreHistory: Marshall was historically also associated with the name Langford. Period photographs preserved in Boulder County watershed history identify the Marshall Coal Mine near Langford in the late nineteenth century.

Remnant uses the documented Marshall Mesa mining landscape as the identification point for this broad historic complex rather than claiming a particular surviving underground opening. Historic mine workings are extensive and some coal seams remain active underground; visitors should remain on designated public routes.

The 1883 Fox Mine Office is a documented surviving building associated with coal mining in the Marshall area. The broader Marshall Mesa trail landscape includes interpretive information about local coal-mining and geologic history.
